geometry.units: um; x along the bus, y across it; ring 0 at the origin
geometry.ring_radius_note: r_ref of the model (R3: the radius that gives the 1.8 THz FSR with the solver's group index)

heater_annulus_um.note: in-ring doped-silicon heater inside the rib, placed as the model's FEM extraction assumes (heater_gap 2 um, width 1 um; assumed); the plant itself treats each ring's heater as a lumped source at its centre

geometry.waveguide_note: drawn, not modelled: the plant has no waveguide layout (the bus loss uses the 50 um ring spacing); bus and drop centre lines from r_ref, the rib width and the coupling gaps of the coupler extraction (183 nm through, 382 nm drop); light enters at the left (x < 0) and passes ring 0 first
geometry.aggressor_note: 'aggressor' is the default A1/A2 site (30 um from ring 0, 55 um from its PD, the same point as ring 0's driver site); 'aggressor_pd_adjacent' is a stress site only
geometry.temp_sensor_note: die0 sits 1 mm from the bank centroid, outside the maps

heater_structure.note: the heater body of the preset's heater family (ring.thermal.family) as the model's FEM extraction draws it (mrm.extraction.thermal_fem.ThermalConfig.heater_rects: axisymmetric annuli, r from the ring centre, z from the bottom of the silicon film), at the model's ring radius r_ref. Assumed: the G26 heater type and position are unpublished (preset coverage 'metal/heater geometry'). The plant treats the heater as a lumped source.

site_sizes_um.note: the radii the FEM extraction gives these sites (ThermalConfig; assumed); the plant itself uses point sites

distances.note: centre to centre unless the name says edge; from the preset's site positions (all assumed)

lasers.note: line 0 is the reddest; ring n is designed for line n (ring_to_line); the cold start's supervisor may assign another line (declared_line in the traces)

rings.cold_resonance_note: resonance at 25 degC, 0 V bias, heater off (the design is 7.6 nm blue of its line)

scenarios.title: Steady lock
scenarios.description: pi_lock_c holds all 8 rings at 25 °C from a settled warm start, no disturbance (40 ms).

scenarios.title: A1 on-die aggressor
scenarios.description: pi_lock_c under the A1 slide-10 aggressor 30 µm from ring 0, one 130.7 ms period from its cool minimum (hot cusp at 65.35 ms). Ring 0 is heated most; near the cusp its heater runs down to code 0 and the ring leaves its operating point.

scenarios.title: +10 % laser power step
scenarios.description: pi_lock_c at 25 °C; at 10 ms every laser line steps +10 % in power (0.414 dB), the rings heat themselves more and the lock moves its set point.

scenarios.title: Cold start (WDM supervisor)
scenarios.description: wdm_supervisor from a cold start at 25 °C: heaters at 0, lasers ramp on over 3 ms; it sweeps each ring to map the lines, assigns lines (a barrel shift is allowed) and locks the rings one by one, in bus order.

devices.note: the realized plant's settings (nominal world), read from the engine's hardware objects

timing.note: ticks of dt_s. Controller steps at phase + j x period; ADC samples of ring n end at phase[n] + j x adc_period after a window of adc_window ticks and are released adc_latency ticks later; a heater command reaches the DAC output dac_latency ticks after it is latched

thermal_coupling.note: DC gains Z(0) = sum of the lag residues (mrm.plant.thermal.dc_gain), K per mW into the source

full.note: every observer (rings, heater resistors, monitor PDs, die sensor) against every heat source: DC gain Z(0) = sum of the residues (mrm.plant.thermal.dc_gain), K per mW into the source; lags [tau_s, residue K/mW] (step response sum r (1 - exp(-t/tau))); t10/t63/t90: the first time the step response reaches 10 / 63.2 / 90 % of its DC value (none when the DC gain is not positive). The heat transport delay is not applied by the thermal kernels (0 here).

rows.label: DAC code range
rows.note: 16-bit voltage DAC; code 0 = heater off.

rows.label: Full-scale voltage
rows.note: Heater voltage at the highest code: V = code / code_max × V_FS.

rows.label: Maximum power per heater
rows.note: Driver law at full code with the heater at 25 °C (V_FS² / R). It falls as the heater warms (TCR).

rows.label: Resistance temperature coefficient (TCR)
rows.note: R = R0 (1 + TCR × (T_heater − 25 °C)).

rows.label: Bank supply power limit
rows.note: Sum of the 8 heaters; above it the drive is scaled down.

rows.label: Heater power for one FSR
rows.note: Tuning efficiency anchor: the power that moves the resonance by one free spectral range.

rows.label: Bias DAC range
rows.note: Range of the junction bias set point.

rows.label: Bias set point
rows.note: scenario.bias_v: the mean of the two data levels.

rows.label: Data swing
rows.note: Peak to peak, centered on the bias.

rows.label: Junction level 0 (V0)
rows.note: Model output (Truth, steady run, median of the rings): bias − swing / 2.

rows.label: Junction level 1 (V1)
rows.note: Model output (Truth, steady run, median of the rings): bias + swing / 2.

rows.label: Resonance shift V0 → V1
rows.note: Model output (phase model, steady run): level-1 resonance minus level-0 resonance.

rows.label: PD dark current at 25 °C
rows.note: Grows with temperature, activation energy 0.37 eV.

rows.label: ADC full scale (PGA gain 1)
rows.note: Codes 0 to 65535; full scale / gain at higher gains.

rows.label: Input noise
rows.note: Plus shot noise.

rows.label: ADC sample period
rows.note: 250 kHz sample rate.

rows.label: Controller step period
rows.note: controller_interface.update_rate_hz.

rows.label: Controller latency
rows.note: From the latch of the inputs to the command (pi_lock_c).

rows.label: Laser power per line
rows.note: 10 mW at the laser module.

rows.label: Chip input loss
rows.note: Light into the chip: × 0.2512 per line.

rows.label: Receiver sensitivity (OMA at BER 1e-9)
rows.note: -12.8 dBm OMA on every lane: the worst lane of the G26 range -14.0 to -12.8 dBm, read off a plot (mrm.plant.datapath).

rows.label: Link transmission
rows.note: 3 dB chip to chip, bus output to the receiver (LM26-P; the mrm.plant.datapath default).

rows.label: BER limit
rows.note: metrics.ber_limit (the G26 criterion).

hardware_limits.note: the g26 preset's values as the realized plant uses them (nominal world); provenance: the preset's tag for that key, or 'derived' (model output), 'model default' (a module default), 'preset setting' / 'model setting' (no tag)

units.detuning_pm: pm, resonance minus its declared line (positive = red of the line)
units.p_in_mw: mW (light at the ring input on its declared line)
units.reloma_db: dB (OMA / P_in at the ring's through port)
units.oracle_reloma_db: dB (best stable relOMA at that instant)

limits: Every number is the g26 preset's nominal world: many inputs are assumed, inferred or from imec and G25 devices, not from a measured G26 die (docs/EXPLAINED.md).

The thermal map is the model's lumped point-site law (one pole per source and distance), not a 3-D field solve; it is exact at the monitor PDs (same law) and under-reads near and inside a ring, whose temperature is its own lumped observer (ring_rise_k).
The heat dynamics come from imec measurements and assumptions (natural-convection package); G26's own time constants and crosstalk are unknown.
Spectra use the model's rigid-comb phase model: a heated ring keeps its cold FSR (the locked order is exact; adjacent orders are off by up to about 33 pm at the lock).
Waveguides, heater annuli and coupling gaps are drawn from the model's extraction inputs; the plant itself has no layout beyond the site positions.
